chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever has intercourse with a woman once, and then is taken back to her (in the marriage), she has no right of option (khayar).'

key_terms.أُخِّذَ: Taken back (referring to revocation of conditional divorce or re-taking)
key_terms.خِيَار: Option/Right of choice (specifically in marriage context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's right of option (khayar) after consummation and re-taking in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Sakuni from Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies the legal status of 'khayar al-ruju' (the right of return) in the context of conditional divorce (tadlis). It establishes that once consummation has occurred, the wife's right to unilaterally dissolve the marriage upon the husband's return is extinguished, aligning with the principle that consummation solidifies the marital bond. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between pre-consummation and post-consummation rights in temporary or conditional marital arrangements.
